scope: CGB-001 short-term HR-TFT optical response and the bounded family ensemble used when no authentic CGB waveform or GtG matrix is available.
rules: Sharp's 6.5-inch GH/HCR prototype values bound a period-family ensemble; they are not CGB measurements.
The source labels response only as on and off or gray scales. Direction, threshold definition, temperature, waveform, and the gray pair are not silently invented as source facts.
A common project-equivalent 10-to-90 definition may parameterize candidate equations only when that conversion is explicitly classified as period-reconstructed.
No channel multiplier, temperature coefficient, overshoot, overdrive, or hidden LC state is selected without transferable CGB evidence.
WS1 supplies settled fixed-angle color endpoints; WS4 may not edit, resample, or replace the WS1 LUT.
Short-term optical response remains separate from WS7 VCOM/residual-DC retention.

items.title: Development of HR-TFT (High Reflective-TFT)
claimsUsed: period Sharp reflective active-matrix a-Si HR-TFT prototypes were not instantaneous
HCR is the faster family endpoint and GH is the slower family endpoint in the reported table
gray-scale response is slower than on-and-off response for both reported modes
items.limits: Different 6.5-inch prototype with no identified CGB relationship. The paper does not define the timing thresholds, separate rise/fall, name a gray pair, give temperature, publish waveforms, or provide a GtG matrix.

items.title: Current Status and Trends of Reflective Liquid Crystal Displays
claimsUsed: period reflective HCR construction uses a single-polarizer reflective architecture
reflective optical endpoints depend on the complete LC, filter, and reflector path
items.limits: Architecture context only; it supplies no transferable CGB response waveform, direction split, GtG value, or temperature coefficient.

items.title: Overdrive Method for Reducing Response Times of Liquid Crystal Displays
claimsUsed: gray-to-gray nematic response can depend on transient director dynamics and addressing history
hydrodynamic flow and multiplexed addressing can be material when modeling an overdriven TN response
a richer recursive or multi-state candidate is scientifically plausible but needs waveform evidence
items.limits: Not a CGB or Sharp HR-TFT measurement. It supplies no transferable CGB milliseconds, state coefficients, overdrive behavior, or evidence that the CGB uses overdrive.

items.title: Pinned HCS GBC reflectance measurement and WS1 color reduction
claimsUsed: settled code endpoints are evaluated through the accepted fixed-angle WS1 color model
all response members must settle to byte-identical WS1 model-space color
items.limits: The HCS source contains static patch readings and no temporal waveform, GtG matrix, temperature sweep, or scan-synchronized optical capture.

items.title: CGB-001 WS3 bounded scan-drive contract
claimsUsed: the response integrator uses the exact selected frame duration
response state is pixel-local and receives no future source frame
items.limits: WS3 does not measure LC response or identify a family mode.

items.title: Authentic CGB temporal-response data gap
items.result: No accepted source provides an original CGB waveform, threshold definition, per-channel 32x32 GtG matrix, direction split, overshoot, temperature coefficient, or specimen distribution.
items.limits: Absence from the accepted source set does not prove that future synchronized photodiode measurements or a panel specification cannot be obtained.
